Real-time audio streaming demands high fidelity and low latency, as emphasized by Werner and Kraneis. However, Besjedica et al. highlighted that traditional VLC systems often struggle to maintain consistent data rates in environments with unstable lighting conditions, leading to signal degradation and variable latencies. Raj et al. proposed adaptive modulation techniques and dynamic beam steering as potential solutions to these challenges, though their operational complexity raises feasibility concerns.

Interference remains a critical challenge for VLC systems, as noted by Ibhaze et al.. Environmental factors, including natural and artificial lighting, introduce noise that degrades signal integrity. Sanusi et al. explored narrow-band optical filters for reducing interference from ambient light sources, improving the SNR. Beamforming algorithms, as investigated by Nor and Mohamed, show promise in directing light beams more accurately, thereby mitigating interference. However, the constraint of commercialization significantly limit the further exploration with this hardware.

High-fidelity audio transmission over VLC systems have two essential criteria. The first criteria is the high SNR and the second criteria are the low BER. The adaptive modulation schemes developed by Salvi et al. balances between these criteria. Instead of focusing on balancing these two criteria, Shu et al. focused on error correction codes, such as Reed-Solomon, in reducing BER. These approaches have been proven as effective. However, the lack to seamless integration ability to transform these technologies into a feasible system is a major limitation.

The limitations and scope of improvement discovered through the literature review addresses the need for comprehensive solutions provided in this paper. This study aims to bridge the gaps identified in the literature review by proposing a novel VLC transceiver design with interference-resilient protocols optimized for real-time audio and music streaming applications.

With the goal of secure and efficient communications, the VLC Consortium (VLCC) was established to promote and standardize VLC technology in 2007. The former is a combination of UFSOOK and VPPM, wherein VPPM is achieved by changing the duty cycle of high rate pulses. The term "twinkle" in the twinkle VPPM stems from the LED lights being perceived as flashing rapidly on the RX. On the other hand, HS-PSK is a combination of both S2-PSK and dimmable spatial multiple-PSK (DSM-PSK). In this study, the Osram DURIS E5 LED, with a peak wavelength at 450 nm and a broad spectrum extending beyond the blue range, posed unique challenges for interference reduction. To address this, the narrow-band optical filter was optimized to primarily focus on the blue wavelength of the LED. This approach minimizes interference from other portions of the spectrum while retaining most of the signal power from the transmitter. The central wavelength of the filter is set to 450 nm with a bandwidth of 20 nm, aligning with the Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) of the transmitter's emission spectrum. The blue portion of the spectrum is less affected by low-frequency ambient interference, as most artificial light sources emit higher intensity in the yellow-to-red range. Focusing on the blue wavelength ensures compatibility with the photodetector's sensitivity range and maximizes the SNR. The effectiveness of this filter design is validated through simulations and experiments, showing that it reduces interference from both white Gaussian shot noise and low-frequency ambient noise. • Minimum EM interference: VLC generates almost no EM radiation in space, which provides a good wireless communication solution for environments with EM interference sensitive devices or where radio silence is required.

• Signal secrecy: Due to the long wavelength and antenna architecture, RF communication presents weak directionality and can be easily tracked by non-target receivers. In VLC, since the light wavelength is short, light is subject to directionality and attenuation effects and cannot penetrate walls when it propagates in space. Thus, light can only be received in a specific area and the confidentiality of transmitted information is ensured.

• Energy efficiency: Compared to traditional light sources, LEDs present higher electro-optic conversion efficiency. If LEDs can be used to provide communication services while lighting, they will definitely save a lot of energy. Therefore, the concept of integrated lighting communication has also been proposed. Furthermore, compared to RF femtocell networks, VLC systems could achieve a very large area spectral efficiency gain.

• Health safety: Compared with infrared radiation (IR) communications, an improper application of IR can cause damage to the human body due to the high temperature since IR is a kind of heat radiation. For example, strong IR rays can cause skin burns or damage the retina of the fundus. Under normal lighting conditions, the use of VLC does not pose any safety problems for the human body.

• Pervasive infrastructure (LEDs): Due to the gradual widespread adoption of LEDs as the fourth generation of lighting technology, lighting facilities represent a natural platform for VLC. Furthermore, wavelength dependency becomes an even more important factor when considering color-domain-based VLC systems, in which the wavelength dependence of the channel is crucial to the system's performance. The most notable color-domain-based modulation scheme is known as color shift keying (CSK) modulation, in which data are encoded into the instantaneous optical power of RGB LEDs in such a way that the perceived color and the average transmitted optical are static. This modulation scheme is included in the IEEE 802.15.7 standard for high-data-rate applications with multiple light sources, where 4-CSK, 8-CSK, and 16-CSK constellations are defined. Most of the existing literature on the performance and channel modeling of CSK-based VLC systems considers classical indoor VLC channels with only a line-of-sight (LOS) component. Notable exceptions include the outdoor optical camera communications channel (OOC), the underwater optical communication channel (UWOOC), and the underwater wireless optical communication channel (UWOC). To the best knowledge of the authors, CSK-based UM-VLC systems have not been modeled or evaluated in the literature so far.

The authors proposed a refractive index optimization of the RIS element to improve user fairness. The smooth control of light propagation is given by the reorientation of LC molecules through voltage control.

The study formulates a user-fairness optimization problem based on the achievable rate of each user on the receiving plane in an indoor environment served by an LC-RIS transmitter. As the problem is non-convex, PSO is used to find the optimal refractive index by optimization.

Simulations were conducted in a 5x5x3 m room, with a centralized LED located at a height of 0.85 meters above the floor. The room was divided into a 100 × 100 grid. The results compare PSO with the SCA algorithm. Both algorithms converge to FI = 1 (representing the best fairness) before three iterations. Comparing LC-RIS optimized by PSO and non-RIS, PSO optimization improved around 31% at 1 W optical power or 7% at 5 W under the same conditions. The sum-rate RIS LoS + NLoS increased up to 233% at 2 W optical power. The results also show that the scheme achieves up to a 53% rate improvement when the incident light wavelength decreases from 670 nm to 510 nm. LEDs generate light based on an electroluminescence phenomenon that occurs when an electric field is applied to a P-N junction, promoting the recombination of electrons and holes. Since LEDs are made with direct semiconductor materials, the recombination generates photons in a determined wavelength and heat. The LED implementation for lighting applications is normally executed with a semiconductor GaN die, which emits blue light that excites a phosphor. A part of the blue photons travels through the phosphor layer without alteration, whereas the rest are converted into yellow photons. Therefore, the white light that is finally emitted by the LED is a combination of blue and yellow photons. Due to their nature, LEDs are power efficient, environmentally friendly, and reliable. For these reasons, LEDs have become strong in the lighting market compared to traditional lighting solutions. In addition, they provide an essential characteristic to enable VLC implementation: the intensity of the light emitted by a LED can be modulated significantly quickly.

section_heading: Harvesting Energy and Data Using Emerging PV Technologies
text: Not much longer from the first proof of concept reported in, the high power conversion efficiencies of emerging PV technologies under indoor environments brought up fascinating questions concerning their communication performances in SLIPT contexts. As early as mid-2015, Zhang et al. used a state-of-the-art organic solar cell for simultaneous energy harvesting and data reception. The 8 mm 2 OPV, based on PTB7:PC 71 BM active layer, performed amazingly well, achieving a 7% PCE under AM 1.5G solar simulator, with a 0.75 V V OC, a 14.6 mA/cm 2 J SC and a FF of 63.8%. It was then attached to the first ever developed reception circuit (as shown in Figure 2b) and, using a red LD with 8.5 mW output power over a 1 m distance, the OFDM-based system reached 34.2 Mbit/s with 4.08 × 10 -4 BER at the MPP, while generating 0.43 mW output electrical power. This was, in fact, the first PV-based VLC system that achieved data rates higher than 12 Mbit/s, but the reason why it performed better is still a question. One may deduce that greater data rates came with the smaller active area of the device, implying a reduced geometric capacitance and, finally, a reduced response time, while others claim that the drift velocity of organic materials is higher than the ones found in Si-based materials, resulting in an increase in the receiver's bandwidth. However, no detailed studies have been proposed since then.

The extra-wide wavelength range of visible light signal from 380 nm to 780 nm can cause a difference of 1.74 dB on the path loss at d = 4.60 m. OOK is one of the most fundamental modulation techniques in VLC, where the intensity of the light source is modulated to represent binary data. In this scheme, the light is turned on to represent a binary '1' and off to represent a binary '0'. This system, employing Manchester-based OOK signals, was designed to prevent the spread of emerging diseases by reducing the need for physical connectivity in highly sterile environments. The field of e-healthcare has experienced significant growth, due to its ability to enable remote patient monitoring, telemedicine consultations, and efficient exchange of medical data among healthcare professionals. Wireless communication technologies are increasingly being integrated into medical body area networks, to enhance flexibility and convenience for caregivers and patients. However, traditional solutions that rely on RF technologies face several challenges, including electromagnetic interference with precision medical equipment, saturation of the radio spectrum, and limited bandwidth. VLC emerges as an innovative alternative that utilizes white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) for both information transmission and illumination. In this context, VLC offers distinct advantages over RF communications, operating in a different part of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths between 380 and 750 nm and frequencies ranging from 430 to 790 THz-10,000 times larger than the entire RF spectrum. This frequency range is safe for human exposure, does not interfere with sensitive electronic devices, and is not licensed, providing abundant free bandwidth. Additionally, the VLC is energy-efficient, as it uses LEDs for communication and lighting.

• Related challenges and future research directions Due to the limited camera's frame LED pulse rates, the OCC telecommunication system faces a challenge related to synchronization, which happens due to the camera frame. LED flickering, which is known as an undesired light illumination, is considered to be one of the challenges in the VOLUME 9, 2021 OCC system. LED flickering is happened due to the limited camera frame rate. Therefore, further research investigation is required in order to find a feasible way to address the synchronization and light flickering problems in OCC systems. In this context, advanced modulation sachems might be essential to overcome these issues. Furthermore, due to the LoS nature in OCC systems, i.e., no multipath diversity is available, the signals could be subject to block by objects, which prevents light penetration, and thus, could result in losing the connection. Therefore, further investigation is needed to address this technical issue in the OCC system.

section_heading: Challenges and Future Directions for Hybrid VLC/RF Networks
text: The growing dependence on communication technologies and the need to protect the integrity and confidentiality of the information being transmitted makes security mechanisms in hybrid VLC/RF networks of vital importance today. Multiple vulnerabilities and security risks can arise from the use of different communication technologies in hybrid VLC/RF networks. Therefore, it is necessary to develop security mechanisms that protect the privacy of the information transmitted, prevent unauthorized interception of data, and prevent attacks and malicious manipulation. These security mechanisms should include data encryption techniques, user and device authentication, and intrusion detection and prevention. In addition, the integrity of transmitted data must be guaranteed, while access and control policies must be established to ensure that only authorized users can access the network.

section_heading: C. COMPARISON OF RF AND VLC TECHNOLOGIES
text: • Communication and lighting integration: As a communication and lighting integration technology, indoor VLC must balance the dual user requirements of lighting and communication. The transmission of information in VLC relies on changing the luminous intensity, and flickering may occur during communication, which is not allowed in daily lighting and can seriously affect the user's lighting experience. VLC needs to meet the corresponding lighting requirements in both lightings on and lighting off modes.
